brief: A seven-cell honeycomb standing on at least three stud spikes facing down as feet.
costSource: token-equivalent at Muse Spark Open shared rates, info only: the Dedicated Endpoint bills GPU seconds while up (.spend/modal-dedicated.jsonl)

requirements.evidence: 7 full bases placed at 0,0,0 centre + 6 around it: piece:0,0,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full, piece:1,-1,0;full, piece:0,-1,0;full, piece:-1,0,0;full, piece:-1,1,0;full, piece:0,1,0;full — forms complete hexagonal honeycomb, verified by measure 478x501mm and check_build meshClash clear

requirements.requirement: Standing on at least three stud spikes facing down as feet
requirements.evidence: 3 spikes of variant stud facing down: spike:0#-1,0|-1,1|0,0 and spike:0#0,-1|0,0|1,-1 and spike:0#0,0|0,1|1,0 — each at a junction of three cells, positioned under the honeycomb to act as feet; house rules applied (capOpenFaces + lockJoints) without affecting feet

finish.summary: Built 7-cell honeycomb (centre + ring) standing on 3 stud spikes facing down. Verified clear mesh and capped/locked joints for stability.

lines.label: M6 brass heat-set insert, 7.6 mm (initeq M6-1.0 Short)
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

result.note: A spike stands where three bases meet at a corner: place three bases around one junction first. No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.

events.text: You've got a single cell to start — I'll expand that into the full seven.
